newsitem.title: USA: U.S. winter wheat ratings steady despite dryness.
newsitem.headline: U.S. winter wheat ratings steady despite dryness.

text.p: Most U.S. winter wheat remained in mostly good to excellent condition in early January despite some concerns about lack of snow cover and dryness in the hard red winter wheat belt, according to weekly reports issued by the agricultural statistics services in major wheat states.

KANSAS - As of the end of December, winter wheat was rated 82 percent good to excellent, 17 percent fair, and one percent poor, compared to ratings of 90 percent good to excellent, nine percent fair and one percent poor at the start of December. A lack of precipitation across most of the state in December resulted in "dry surface moisture" in western areas.

"This has created a potential blowing problem for some fields, although wind damage has been very light across the state in December," the Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service said. "The wheat lacks snow cover across the state but little freeze damage has occurred to date."
The clear weather has allowed cows and stockers to remain on wheat, corn and milo stubble, the report said.
TEXAS - The Texas winter wheat crop as of January 5 was rated five percent excellent, 47 percent good, 34 percent fair, 13 percent poor and one percent very poor.
"Unseasonably warm and windy conditions ushered in the new year after several weeks of near record lows in many parts of Texas," the state's agricultural statistics service said.

Rainfall was limited in the latest week and "many areas could use a good rain at this point," it said. "Moisture was short in parts of north central Texas but for the most part the remainder of the state had at least some measurable precipitation the past few weeks," the agency said.
Overall, it rated wheat condition statewide at 72 percent of normal compared to 55 percent a year ago.

OKLAHOMA - Dry weather throughout December caused a slight fall in wheat ratings, the state's agricultural statistics service said. As of January 6, wheat was rated three percent excellent, 75 percent good, 21 percent fair, one percent poor.

"Moisture is needed in most areas to continue proper development. Insect pressures are reported light in most areas," the agency said. Wheat acres being grazed were reported at 40 percent against 15 percent last year and the five-year average of 36 percent. Topsoils were rated 28 percent short or one percent very short of moisture. Subsoils were rated 12 percent short or very short.
NEBRASKA - Winter wheat was rated five percent excellent, 56 percent good, 34 percent fair and five percent poor.

"The lack of snow cover and extremely cold weather in December have been a source of concern for winter wheat," the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service said. More moisture was needed in the southwest, which received less than .25 inch of moisture in the month of December. In contrast, the east and north received more than one inch in the month.

MISSOURI - Precipitation in December was below normal except in the Bootheel and at month's end, winter wheat was rated five percent excellent, 43 percent good, 45 percent fair and seven percent poor, down from a month earlier. But soil moisture was not rated short in any area except north-central.
ILLINOIS - As of January 3, winter wheat was rated 10 percent excellent, 61 percent good, 24 percent fair and five percent poor, that state's agricultural statistics service said.
"Many reporters stated that the winter wheat crop is bare and susceptible to damage if the weather turns much colder," the agency said of Illinois wheat.
Note: Indiana and Ohio crop reports were unavailable.
